issue: When a district court allows a defendant to proceed pro se at a supervised release revocation hearing, what standard of appellate review applies to whether the defendant validly waived the statutory right to counsel: abuse of discretion, harmless error, or de novo?

sides.position: Abuse of discretion review applies to a district court's decision to allow a defendant to proceed pro se in a supervised release revocation proceeding.
cases: United States v. Owen, 854 F.3d 536 (8th Cir. 2017)
United States v. Boultinghouse, 784 F.3d 1163 (7th Cir. 2015)
United States v. Walton, No. 23-4314 (4th Cir. 2025)

sides.position: Harmless error review applies to a pro se waiver issue in a supervised release revocation proceeding.
cases: United States v. Spangle, 626 F.3d 488 (9th Cir. 2010)

sides.position: De novo (plenary) review applies because whether the defendant knowingly and voluntarily waived the statutory right to counsel is a question of law.
cases: United States v. Manuel, 732 F.3d 283 (3d Cir. 2013)

this_court: abuse of discretion (majority adopts this standard; the dissent would instead join the Third Circuit and apply de novo review)
quote: A. Before today, this Court has not opined on the proper standard of review when a district court allows a defendant to proceed pro se in a supervised release revocation, and our sister courts have split on this question.
cite: United States v. Eric Walton, No. 23-4314 (4th Cir. 2025)
